first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that reducing onboarding or signup friction improves completion, time-to-value, and first-week activation. This direction best addresses both current declines without the known retention risk of promotional pricing. Verification should confirm experiment design, segment applicability, durability, and whether gains translated beyond early adoption into qualified revenue.

final.rationale: Run a self-serve SMB onboarding simplification experiment. Exp_86 directly supports the current problem, with completion +13%, faster time-to-value, and 30-day retention +3%. Exp_31 confirms SMB activation and qualified-revenue gains, but its 30-day retention decline of 1% warrants explicit retention guardrails. Limit the experiment to the validated SMB context and measure completion, activation, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention. Promotional pricing is not preferred because inherited evidence shows material retention harm despite near-term competitive pressure.
